good_ending_plus

← Back to Reading MAM-parsed-plus

Four books of the Bible end with a verse of rather negative tone. There is a tradition that prevents these verses from being the last verses recited. The tradition is to recite the next-to-last verse after reciting the last verse. To facilitate this tradition, some publications repeat the next-to-last verse, in unpointed form, after the officially-last verse. The good_ending_plus key captures this: it is null for most books. For the 4 book39s that have it (Isaiah, Malachi, Lamentations, Ecclesiastes), it is an object (see example below).

The template מ:סיום בטוב nested in wikitext_element has separate documentation on its dedicated page.

Example object

Example from Isaiah (book39 level). The good_ending_plus object includes last_chapnver and wikitext_element.

 3  "wikitext_element": {

 5    "tmpl_params": {
 6      "1": {
 7        "tmpl_name": "מ:סיום בטוב",
 8        "tmpl_params": {
 9          "1": "והיה מדי ... אמר יהוה"
10        }
11      },
12      "2": "=מנהג יפה ... בכתי\"ל)."
13    }
14  }
15}
Line 9
Unpointed text of 66:23 (the next-to-last verse of Isaiah)
Line 12
